objections.text: The hand-derived -5 case already supplies a two-character negative integer and requires the sign after six padding zeros. A01 changes only the digit from 5 to 1 and attacks the same input class and mechanism.

The hand-derived -9999999 case already supplies an eight-character negative integer, including the sign, and requires it unchanged. A02 is the same length class and attacks the same boundary behavior.

The hand-derived -10000000 case already supplies a nine-character negative integer and requires CONVERT(varchar(8), int) to produce '*' before padding. A03 attacks the same length and conversion path.
The hand-derived 12345678 and 99999999 cases already supply eight-character positive integers and require them unchanged. A04 is the same length boundary and does not add a distinct attack mechanism.
The hand-derived int-maximum case already exercises a positive value above eight characters and requires '0000000*'. Moving one below the maximum uses the same conversion and padding path.
The hand-derived int-minimum case already exercises a negative value above eight characters and requires '0000000*'. Moving one above the minimum uses the same conversion and padding path.
